newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday July 24.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema confirmed former star anti-graft magistrate Antonio Di Pietro would run for a seat in the upper house Senate for the governing centre-left coalition. Di Pietro would offer a moderate voice inside the majority coalition (all).

* In an interview, Giorgio Fossa, the head of Italian employers' organisation Confindustria, admitted the economic situation was getting slightly better but said targets were still out of sight and suggested that prime minister Romano Prodi should stop promising and start acting (La Stampa)

* Italian shares surged to new record highs on Wednesday, with the all-share Mibtel index closing 1.56 percent higher and hitting a fresh high of 15,163. The Italian September BTP LIFFE future also hit a fresh all-time high at 138.44, with the spread between cash 10-year BTPs and German bunds narrowing to a record low of 79 basis points (all).
* The Italian Exchange Office said Italy had a 2.549 trillion lire global trade surplus in May compared with 2.736 trillion lire in April (all).

* A report by market research firm Dataquest showed Olivetti's computer systems company Olsy is ranked as Europe's leading supplier of distributed information technology services for the fourth year running in 1996 (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Tecnimont, the engineering arm of Montedison, said it had won a contract worth $180 million for the construction of a petrochemical plant at Triunfo in Brazil (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Energy group ENI said it was re-advertising for bidders for its Pertusola Sud zinc producing unit at Crotone. It said advertisments would be placed in the national and international press (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
